claims.statement: 2FA is extra login security and strongly recommended, with a source-defined cloud mandatory cohort notified for a 45-day enrollment period. Dated notification prose and absent mail do not establish current applicability or excuse an independently imposed organization requirement.

The concept's claim that only password plus phone code can sign in is narrower than its own security-key, Mobile and passwordless passkey alternatives. Preserve this inconsistency; code-on-phone must not become the sole accepted authentication method.

After TOTP or cloud SMS enrollment, alternative WebAuthn keys, optional passkeys and cloud Mobile may be added. Passkeys satisfy password and 2FA, with fallback recommended for lockout prevention; protocol/device capability does not prove enrollment or fresh successful authentication.

Recovery-code storage and additional methods guard against lockout, but exhausted cloud recovery can be permanent and email unlinking is not restored account custody. Source warning and file download cannot certify recoverability.

Owners may require 2FA for organization members, cloud billing managers and outside collaborators. GHES matrix distinguishes built-in/LDAP appliance-managed 2FA, built-in with IdP dependent support, and SAML/CAS unsupported native 2FA that may be supported by the external provider; organization-level 2FA enforcement is unavailable for SAML/CAS. Missing native capability is not permission to waive the security objective.

Browser 2FA and API/CLI credentials differ: the cloud checkup branch describes token/application/SSH access, while browser proof may use code, cloud Mobile, key or passkey. CLI success cannot certify a browser 2FA challenge or organization enforcement.

After password sign-in, secondary proof is needed again for logout, new device, sensitive action or expired session according to the source. Sensitive-action sudo mode is linked separately; existing session presence does not prove fresh proof or authorize changes.

TOTP apps generate codes, but deleting the app may need recovery codes or restored backup. The guide's broad recovery-code wording must preserve separately configured alternative recovery paths; an installed app or backup feature is not restore evidence.

Ordinary security-key sign-in begins with username/password, supported browser and connected key, then presence/PIN/biometric prompt. A passkey instead satisfies both requirements in one step; a key label alone cannot establish credential type or capabilities.

Cloud SMS delivers codes; cloud Mobile push can require a displayed two-digit match, with approve completing and reject preventing sign-in. An unexpected notification is not authority to approve, and delivery is not a successful authenticated session.

GHES 2FA removes account-password CLI authentication, with GCM, PAT or SSH alternatives. The HTTPS PAT-as-password paragraph is narrower than adjacent GCM guidance; do not require newly issued PATs universally, grant broad scopes or record tokens in evidence.

Enabling 2FA leaves SSH authentication unchanged; this does not imply SSH private-key custody, permission scope, SSO approval or effective 2FA gate on every resource. Failed-code errors lead to method troubleshooting before recovery, not a bypass or guessed success.

Enrollment uses TOTP across products or SMS on FPT/GHEC, then alternate security keys. TOTP/cloud-backed backup recommendation is source guidance, not authority to select a provider, install software, expose a seed or claim provider restore works.

The 28-day checkup feature is cloud-only: successful 2FA exits it, otherwise an existing session prompts on day 28 and provides reconfiguration if proof fails. Configuration form completion alone does not certify durable 2FA, and reconfiguration is not an agent-authorized bypass.

Within that cloud branch, managed users other than the setup user cannot configure account 2FA; an administrator configures IdP 2FA. Setup-user special scope must not grant every managed user local enrollment or agent control of the IdP.

Disabling can remove organization access; outside collaborators can additionally lose private-fork access and need re-enabled 2FA plus owner restoration. Reconfiguration without disabling is the preservation path; source restoration language is not an observed access receipt.

Resolved TOTP setup opens Settings, Password and authentication, Enable 2FA, scans QR or enters setup secret, verifies code, downloads/stores recovery codes and explicitly acknowledges saved codes to enable. Code custody and independent authentication verification are distinct; no seeds/codes enter evidence.

Multiple TOTP devices require scanning at setup or retaining the same secret, with reconfiguration for later device additions. These devices share a secret, so device count alone does not establish independent compromise domains. Manual parameters specify SHA1/six digits/thirty seconds without authorizing changes elsewhere.

Cloud SMS enrollment requires receivable texts, country support, CAPTCHA, number and code verification, then secure recovery-code acknowledgement. Carrier rates and interception/phishing/delivery risks remain; organizations/enterprises may block SMS-enabled members' content access and disallow SMS for outside collaborators.

The passkey-as-2FA procedure requires existing TOTP or cloud SMS and resolved passkey registration with existing-method authentication and success confirmation. General passkey management permits non-2FA use, so this prerequisite belongs to this enrollment path, not a universal passkey prohibition.

Non-passkey WebAuthn security keys verify presence but are secondary factors used with password, unlike user-validating passkeys. Registration requires existing TOTP/cloud SMS, compatible connected key, name, activation and recovery-code custody; enrollment intent is not success.

Cloud Mobile uses public-key authentication after TOTP/SMS setup, application installation/sign-in and enabled push notifications. Existing fallback methods remain relevant; Mobile installation or push enablement alone does not prove the correct account is enrolled or recoverable.
